readme: Reviewed exceptions to the JavaScript dependency advisory gate. See .claude/rules/dependency-security.md before editing. Checked by scripts/audit-gate.mjs.

exceptions.rationale: image-size is Metro's asset-dimension reader: it parses image headers while the bundler resolves assets, and behind the dev-server asset endpoint under `expo start`. It reaches the production graph only because Metro is a transitive dependency of react-native and expo — no Metro code is in a release bundle, which carries the computed dimensions rather than the parser. The images it parses are the assets committed to this repository; the dev-server path exists on a developer machine only and is not present in any shipped build. Metro declares `image-size: ^1.0.2` and resolves 1.2.1, the newest release of the 1.x line (npm's `legacy` tag). The advisory names `>=2.0.3` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 2.0.2, itself inside the vulnerable range — so no `overrides` entry can close this; the only fix on offer would be forcing Metro across a major.

Same package and same reachability as GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq: Metro's bundle-time and dev-server image-header parser, reachable through react-native and expo but absent from every release bundle, and fed only by assets committed to this repository. Metro declares `image-size: ^1.0.2` and resolves 1.2.1, the newest release of the 1.x line (npm's `legacy` tag). The advisory names `>=2.0.3` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 2.0.2, itself inside the vulnerable range — so no `overrides` entry can close this; the only fix on offer would be forcing Metro across a major.

node-forge is reached only through @expo/cli: `expo run:ios` code-signing helpers (`run/ios/codeSigning/Security.js`) and the dev-server manifest signing in `utils/codesigning.js`, which signs the manifests the dev client fetches during `expo start`. The advisory is in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature *verification*; the CLI only signs and generates certificates, and verification of EAS Update manifests happens natively in expo-updates, not in this package. @expo/cli is a developer-machine tool pulled in transitively by `expo` and is in no release bundle. The advisory names `>=1.4.1` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 1.4.0 — so the existing `node-forge@1` override cannot close it; drop this entry once 1.4.1 is published and the override picks it up.

paths: apps/mobile > react-native > @react-native/community-cli-plugin > metro > metro-file-map > micromatch > braces
exceptions.rationale: braces is micromatch's brace-expansion step, reached in two places: eslint-plugin-boundaries at the repository root (lint only) and Metro's file map (`metro-file-map`, `@expo/metro-file-map`), which crawls the project tree while the bundler runs. It is in the production graph only because Metro is a transitive dependency of react-native and expo — no Metro or micromatch code is in a release bundle. The advisory is a stack-exhaustion DoS on deeply nested brace patterns, and every pattern braces sees here is written in this repository (eslint and Metro config globs), not supplied by a user or a network. micromatch declares `braces: ^3.0.3` and resolves 3.0.3, the newest release; the advisory names `>=3.0.4` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 3.0.3 — so no `overrides` entry can close this. Drop this entry once 3.0.4 is published.

extract-zip is the unpacker @electron/packager runs once per `electron-forge package`/`make` to unzip the Electron binary it downloaded from GitHub releases into the bundle; it executes on a developer machine or the CI packaging job only and ships in no app. The archive it opens is the official Electron release zip for the pinned version, not user input. The advisory names `>=2.0.2` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 2.0.1 — so no `overrides` entry can close this.

Same package and same reachability as GHSA-7pqw-9j4j-h8q3: @electron/packager's one-shot unpacker for the official Electron release zip at packaging time, never in a shipped app. No patched version exists on npm (`latest` is 2.0.1), so an override cannot close it.

Reached only through @electron/get, the downloader @electron/packager uses for the Electron binary at packaging time; it runs on a developer machine or the CI packaging job and ships in no app. The fix is 4.3.0, published 2026-10-04, which `minimumReleaseAge` (4 days) refuses until 2026-10-08 — then `'http-cache-semantics@4': '^4.3.0'` goes into `overrides` and this entry is dropped.
